knownMigrationDrift.$comment: ACTIVE drift, measured against the live ledger 2026-09-17. Sixteen migrations were applied to canonical production under different version stamps than the files carry. Content is believed unchanged; only the recorded version differs. This is the mechanical reason the protected one-click migration workflow's drift check cannot pass, and reconciling it is its own approved piece of work. reconstructedFromProduction.$comment: BarberOS was built directly against canonical production between 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-13 and was never committed. Repo ordinals 0049-0054 reconstruct the END STATE of the `barberos` and `transform_audit` schemas read out of the live catalog; they are NOT a replay of production's history, because the live database records what exists, not which migration created which object, and inventing a plausible split would be fabricated history. Both schemas were verified byte-for-byte against production by structural fingerprint -- twelve categories for barberos, eleven for transform_audit (it seeds no catalog rows) -- and every category matched. They are ALREADY APPLIED in production under the names below and MUST NOT be applied there again; their purpose is to make the repository true, to let CI prove the schemas apply from empty, and to give supabase/tests/49_barberos.sql and 53_transform_audit.sql something to test. The eleven production migrations are now fully covered.
reconstructedFromProduction.verificationMethod: Structural fingerprints computed identically on canonical production and on a local PostgreSQL 16.13 with all 54 migrations applied from empty: 12 categories for barberos (columns, constraints, indexes, policies, RLS flags, triggers, functions, function grants, table grants, enums, seeded catalog rows, permissions) and the same 11 for transform_audit. All matched after normalising the `extensions.` schema qualifier, which renders differently under the two sessions' search_path. The comparison found two real divergences that reading the code had not: a missing authenticated grant on the two inner published-site functions, and an EXTRA grant on transform_audit.recompute_composite that production deliberately withholds.
reconstructedFromProduction.knownResidual: In BOTH schemas the trigger functions carry PostgreSQL's built-in default of EXECUTE to PUBLIC (proacl is null), so `anon` can call them: five in barberos and eight in transform_audit. Production is in the same state, so it is reproduced rather than silently corrected -- changing it here would be a behaviour change smuggled in under a reconciliation. It is inert: a trigger function cannot be called outside a trigger, which 49_barberos.sql asserts. Worth a separate, deliberate migration across both schemas. The transform_audit public-API gap this section previously recorded is ADDRESSED by migration 0055 (22 public.barberos_audit_* RPCs, all SECURITY INVOKER, no anon grant) -- but 0055 is unapplied, so in PRODUCTION those 40 runs, 45 findings and 40 recommendations are still unreadable until it is approved and applied.
